evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/delegations.rs:207-236 — create_delegation only verifies unit ownership INSIDE `if let Some(unit_id) = req.unit_id { ... get_owners_rls ... is_owner ... 403 NOT_OWNER }`. When the client omits `unit_id` (req.unit_id == None), that whole ownership gate is skipped: the handler validates scopes and that the delegate user exists, then calls `delegation_repo.create(auth.user_id, create_data)` with `unit_id: None` and arbitrary scopes (up to `["all"]`) — with NO check that the delegator has any authority to delegate. A caller can thus mint a unit-less delegation to any delegate_user_id.

backend/crates/db/src/repositories/delegation.rs:277-303 — has_delegation() treats a NULL unit_id row as a WILDCARD over every unit: `WHERE delegate_user_id = $1 AND status = 'active' AND (unit_id = $2 OR unit_id IS NULL) AND ($3 = ANY(scopes) OR 'all' = ANY(scopes)) AND start_date <= CURRENT_DATE AND (end_date IS NULL OR end_date >= CURRENT_DATE)`. So the unit-less delegation created above answers `has_delegation(delegate, <ANY unit_id>, <ANY scope>) = true`. The query runs against `&self.pool` directly (not an RLS-scoped connection), so the wildcard is effectively global/cross-tenant, and `'all'` in scopes is itself a second wildcard over the scope check.

Chain: delegations.rs:676-694 check_delegation exposes this via GET /api/v1/delegations/check/{unit_id}/{scope}, which returns `has_delegation: true` for a delegate holding an ownerless unit-less delegation, for units the delegator never owned. Impact today = MEDIUM: has_delegation/check_delegation is currently only consumed by the informational check endpoint (grep confirms no server-side voting/financial/document write yet gates on it), so it is a delegation-model INTEGRITY break (a user can confer authority — voting/financial/documents/faults/all — that they do not themselves hold, over resources they do not own) rather than an already-wired privilege escalation. It becomes a direct broken-access-control escalation the moment any handler starts trusting check_delegation/has_delegation to authorize an action. Confidence HIGH: full path traced entry->issue (create_delegation None branch -> repo create -> has_delegation NULL-wildcard SQL on &self.pool); reachable in production. Fix (backend-only, no schema change needed): in create_delegation require `unit_id` to be Some, OR when it is None constrain the grant to units the delegator actually owns; alternatively narrow has_delegation so a NULL-unit delegation only matches units the DELEGATOR (owner_user_id) owns rather than every unit. Mirror the existing get_owners_rls ownership check already used on the Some(unit_id) branch.
